args.summary: The party met Sela Thorn at Gullwick Docks, explored the flooded Saltmere Mine and found a hymn page marked "M. Brand", then witnessed the drowned bell and pale congregation at midnight. The GM set the Hollow Choir clock to 3/6. Back at the Tarred Gull, the party planned a first-light boat trip and daytime low-tide chapel dive. Teo's identification of Mira's handwriting, suspicions about Maren, Sela's account of the mine flood, the fishermen's Kelp Mother story, and Bram's account of Maren remain attributed claims or plans.

properties.role: Tide reader and boatwoman at pier four
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her; avoids eye contact and watches the tide line. Grey braid and salt-stained coat.
properties.wants: Offers to row the party for two silver, during daylight only; says she will be at pier four tomorrow at first light.
properties.knows: Says Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang forty years ago; attributes the warm floodwater account to her grandmother. Claims hers is the only boat that goes near the bell water.

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye. She keeps her gaze on the tide line.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.
Fine, she'll do it for two silver.
Sella's boat is the only one that goes near the bell water. The others are scared.
Sela, Sella, the dockhands say it both ways.
Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.
She shrugs and goes back to her net. She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Records the new voiced NPC, both spellings, her manner and the offered passage.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.
There's a woman sitting on an upturned skiff, mending a net. Grey braid, salt-stained coat. She doesn't look up.

changes.why: The party met Sela at the docks.

change.name: Did Saltmere flood when the bell first rang?

properties.what_is_open: Sela says Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang forty years ago; her grandmother reportedly said the water came up warm. The timing and cause remain unverified.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Sela's attributed account raises a possible connection between the mine flood and the bell.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Sela supplied the flood lead.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: The account concerns Saltmere Mine.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path. A black entrance in chalk with half-rotted timbers and a rusted cart on its side. Warm air smells of old candle wax. Thirty paces in, warm black water floods the tunnel; wet hymn-book pages float on it and stick to the walls.
properties.state: Closed; tunnel flooded with warm black water about thirty paces inside. The air harmed Oren during the visit.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side. The air coming out of it is warm and smells like a church, like old candle wax.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.
You don't find anything else. Oren, take two damage from the bad air.

changes.why: The party directly observed the mine's condition and hazardous air.

change.name: Hymn page marked M. Brand at Saltmere

properties.statement: At Saltmere Mine, Teo retrieved a wet hymn-book page about the sea giving back what it takes, with "M. Brand" pencilled in the margin.

sources.quote: I fish one out. What's on it?
A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: Records the physical clue without asserting who wrote it.

sources.quote: About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch. Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: The hymn page was found in the mine.

properties.what_changed: A hymn page at Saltmere bears "M. Brand". Teo identifies the handwriting as his sister Mira's and believes she was there; the GM has not confirmed that identification.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: The clue advances Teo's search while keeping his identification a player inference.

change.name: Is Maren involved in the Hollow Choir?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa suspects harbor-master Maren is in a cult and behind the events; Oren suspects she runs the choir. These are player guesses, not established facts.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.
You can think that. Roll investigation if you want to search the rest.

changes.why: Preserves the party's suspicion without changing Maren's established state.

sources.quote: Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

changes.why: Identifies the subject of the speculative thread.

sources.quote: Okay, I bet the harbor-master is behind all this. Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.

changes.why: Vessa raised the suspicion.

properties.details_shown: Sunk in the bay with its bell. At low water the bell tower and two broken arches protrude, with seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight, pale shapes stood in rows on the submerged chapel floor, like a congregation; they disappeared when the bell stopped.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Records the chapel's visible remains and the witnessed shapes.

properties.what_is_open: A fisherman says the Kelp Mother drags children standing too close to the water down by their ankles. The GM attributes this to fishermen's talk; its truth is unresolved.

sources.quote: Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say. They pull their boat up and leave.

changes.why: Keeps the local warning as rumor rather than establishing a creature.

sources.quote: You get back to Gullwick by dusk, and you decide to go down to the shore below the old chapel ruins anyway, Sela's warning or not.
Don't stand that close. The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.

changes.why: The warning was given on the chapel shore.

sources.quote: That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: The GM explicitly advances the existing hidden clock from 2/6 to 3/6.

properties.what_is_open: Who or what rings the drowned bell? It rang twelve times at midnight again, with much louder humming; pale shapes appeared in rows on the submerged chapel floor and vanished when the bell stopped.

sources.quote: And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago. You can feel it in your teeth.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: The party gains direct evidence while the bell-ringer remains unknown.

sources.quote: Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: Connects the bell mystery to the witnessed chapel congregation.

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks, with a fire going and smells of tar and fish stew.
properties.state: The party rested here at the end of the session.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.
Long rest at the inn?
Yes, long rest, you're all back to full. And that's where we stop for tonight.

changes.why: Records the new location and the session's stopping point.

properties.played_as: Huge, with a red beard; laughs at his own jokes and wipes the same mug throughout the conversation. Teases the party as brave or stupid and gives them stew on the house.
properties.knows: Says he has known Maren for thirty years, calls her sharp-tongued but good-hearted, and says she lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.
Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Records the voiced innkeeper's manner and attributed knowledge.

properties.next_step: The party plans to meet Sela at pier four tomorrow at first light, take her boat out, and dive to the chapel at low tide during daylight. Vessa intends to buy rope and a second lantern tonight; purchase and departure are not confirmed.

sources.quote: At low tide, during the day. Not at night, Sela was right about that.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: Records the agreed next step as a plan rather than a completed journey.

change.name: Bram's account of Maren's lost brother

properties.what_is_open: Bram says Maren lost a brother to the bay and describes her as sharp-tongued but good-hearted after thirty years of acquaintance. The circumstances of the loss and its relevance remain unknown.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Bram offers an attributed personal lead about Maren.
